question_text: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Ulnar nerve
opb. Anterior interosseous nerve
opc. Superficial radial nerve
opd. Posterior interosseous nerve
ope. Musculocutaneous nerve

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with pain and weakness in the right forearm and hand, with a history of ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation. Physical examination reveals tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle, marked weakness in extending the right middle finger, and radial deviation during wrist extension. These symptoms suggest dysfunction of the radial nerve, specifically the posterior interosseous nerve, which innervates the wrist extensors and is responsible for finger extension. The history of trauma and the specific weakness pattern align with posterior interosseous nerve involvement, making it the most likely affected nerve in this case.
